      RETAIN IN CORE · #123–128#123Move bytes, keep replacement behavior.Source caching moves from TypeScript to core. A selected snapshot still evicts omitted cached bytes; selection-aware retention is deferred. The PR also rewrites the repository PR template without a recorded bundling reason.↗#124Prepare a candidate; publish only after validation.Core takes revision diffs and portable indexes. TypeScript keeps its mutation journal and exact source handles. Missing-file preparation still commits one file at a time.↗#126Make project membership one publication.Core discovers, observes, validates, and publishes project membership. TypeScript keeps tsconfig and toolchain hooks; FIFO order, inferred fallback, and release order remain explicit choices.↗#127Keep six caches. Give them one lifetime.Core owns clearing, while TypeScript keeps query algorithms, keys, and identities. Clear after successful refresh and synchronously before awaiting release; cached undefined still counts as a hit.↗#128Warm means keeping the same core object.Core sessions own discovery and backend lifetime. Cold runs use request discovery, warm runs retain a catalog, selections discover afresh, each turn gets a router, and release can be repeated.↗NAME THE BOUNDARIES · #129–136#129Resolve the environment once, in the host.State-directory resolution moves from telemetry to CLI. One canonical path feeds both consumers, including paths with missing tails. Fixture synchronization and larger status-test budgets also land here.↗#130Create the package before moving its mechanisms.A dependency-free daemon package owns portable contracts and an immutable, complete policy snapshot. Limits, memory recipes, test overrides, and intentional missing deadlines get a policy record. Mechanisms still live in CLI.↗#131The snapshot becomes the only threshold input.Consumers require policy slices. Status has 100 ms while ordinary lifecycle exchanges have 250 ms. Fetch resumes and accepted reattachments use separate counters; test adapters replace production override seams.↗#132Classify argv once. Carry the name.CLI syntax selects one daemon-owned command identity beside opaque argv. It participates in duplicate compatibility. Protocol generation changes from 4 to 5, with mixed generations taking compatibility handling before execution.↗#133One outer failure vocabulary; a separate worker domain.Daemon owns outer failure codes, validation, and precedence. CLI supplies instanceof facts; worker failures keep their distinct wire values. Accepted terminal failures keep controlled results without local replay.↗#134The first failed guard owns the answer.Authentication, readiness, pressure, draining, and duplicate compatibility are ordered. Authentication failure disconnects; retry safety comes from the rejection code, and conflicting duplicates do not mutate accepted state.↗#135The worker loads its host through a module URL.CLI implements a daemon-defined executor contract. A validated absolute URL crosses process and worker boundaries. Worker code owns sequencing, rechunking, and sampling; diagnostics remain opaque. Two test budgets become 15 s.↗#136Move output bytes to the renderer.One stateless renderer formats public daemon start/status/stop reports. CLI still chooses format, writes output, and wraps errors. Renderer imports the daemon public reports.↗SPLIT THE TRANSPORT · #137–143#137Cut framing out of the transport facade.Operation-shaped ports replace broad concrete dependencies. Codec and validator own binary framing, integrity, and frame-kind limits; facade mapping preserves transport error meaning.↗#138A connection can end before a transfer does.One receiver retains manifest, digest, and durable offsets across reconnections. Capture owns stored output; offsets advance only after append. Decoders are fresh per socket and output disposal transfers to the caller. A test budget grows 20→60 s.↗#139Give every outbound exchange one byte connection.A socket client owns connection timeout, pull-driven reads, FIFO writes, backpressure, and closure. The facade still interprets protocol and delivery state; inbound serving waits for its own step.↗#140Group bounded responses by their shared lifecycle.Lifecycle, execution-status, and result acknowledgement use one client for correlation, deadlines, and cleanup. Acknowledgement stays off the general lifecycle port; semantic validation precedes accepted classification.↗#141Split the other side of the socket.A server owns endpoint probes, listening, per-connection response/write chains, and shutdown. It reuses the socket client for probes; concurrent shutdown callers share settlement and force can escalate a drain.↗#142Recover delivery without replaying accepted work.A dedicated execution client owns admission through acknowledgement. Fetch resumes reuse an attempt’s receiver; identical-request reattachments create a new capture. Numeric budgets remain independent and exhausted fetches retain accepted-corruption meaning.↗#143Leave the transport facade with only wiring.One required policy composes the split owners. Direct component injection preserves returned identity; the canFrame probe disappears. A source-boundary test replaces any temptation to use file length as an architecture rule.↗SPLIT THE PROCESS · #144–147#144Capture state here; project it there.A pure activity projector consumes explicit process, clock, queue, resource, and worker snapshots. It uses the in-progress worker generation and sampled spool bytes, keeps legacy fileCount behavior, and returns frozen values.↗#145One manager owns each generation handoff.Worker startup, execution, replacement, fencing, release, and shutdown move behind a manager. Resource policy stays behind a recovery port. Warm-up sampling gates readiness; replacement is shared, while force can interrupt graceful close.↗#146Coordinate delivery without taking its data.One delivery session coordinates attachment, transfer, acknowledgement, and traces. Ledger and spool keep state and bytes. The latest delivery is the queue barrier; expired traces are fenced, and cleanup failure does not withhold protocol acknowledgement.↗#147Serialize accepted turns over existing owners.An execution session coordinates the FIFO queue, delivery, worker, resources, and lifetime. Immutable metadata stays on ledger entries; sampling gates the next turn. Duplicates attach without a second acceptance or lifetime reset.↗STAGE, THEN SWITCH · #148–149#148Two copies exist. The CLI still runs its old graph.DaemonClient, executable entries, and mechanisms arrive in the package. Its Node-free facade loads a private runtime; lazy routing stops at the first decision. CLI compatibility copies stay active while mechanism tests move. Clocks, registry authority, output ownership, and existing idle timing remain explicit.↗#149Switch the caller. Delete the compatibility graph.CLI invocation coordination calls DaemonClient and package transport composition replaces the old facade. External tests use a read-only inspector and package actors; syntax-aware rules enforce imports, clocks, exports, and storage. Policy serialization becomes private. Ten CLI status/stop scenarios disappear, pressure assertions change, and inspector failure handling is added.↗
